about: Drafts for the 76 events_master.csv rows that matched no existing event (reconcile-events, 2026-11-04). Names and descriptions were written by Claude from the CSV text and general knowledge, NOT verified against sources. Year = CSV year unless the note says otherwise. Difficulty = CSV itemDifficulty mapped 1-4 easy, 5-7 medium, 8-10 hard.

events.name: King David Captures Jerusalem
events.description: According to biblical tradition, King David captures the Jebusite city of Jerusalem and makes it the capital of a united Israelite kingdom. Jerusalem becomes the political and religious centre of the Israelites, a status that later shapes its importance for Judaism, Christianity and Islam.
events.note: Traditional date; usually given as c. 1000 BCE and the historicity is debated.

events.name: Ptolemy I Becomes Pharaoh of Egypt
events.description: Ptolemy, one of Alexander the Great's generals, declares himself king of Egypt and founds the Ptolemaic dynasty. His Greek-speaking dynasty rules Egypt from Alexandria for nearly three centuries, ending with Cleopatra VII.

events.name: Battle of Zama
events.description: The Roman general Scipio Africanus defeats Hannibal near Zama in North Africa, ending the Second Punic War. Carthage gives up its fleet and overseas territories, leaving Rome the dominant power in the western Mediterranean.
events.note: Related: punic-wars (event and span).

events.name: Julius Caesar Invades Britain
events.description: Julius Caesar leads the first Roman military expedition across the English Channel to Britain, returning with a larger force the following year. He does not conquer the island, but his campaigns draw Britain into the Roman world; full conquest comes under Claudius nearly a century later.

events.name: Second Triumvirate Formed
events.description: Mark Antony, Octavian and Marcus Aemilius Lepidus form the Second Triumvirate, a legally sanctioned dictatorship of three men, after Julius Caesar's assassination. They purge their opponents, including Cicero, and defeat Caesar's assassins, but the rivalry between Antony and Octavian later ends the Republic.
events.note: Related: first-triumvirate.

events.name: Jin Dynasty Reunifies China
events.description: The Western Jin dynasty conquers the state of Wu, ending the Three Kingdoms period and reuniting China under Emperor Wu (Sima Yan). The unity is short-lived: within decades civil war and invasions split northern and southern China again.
events.note: CSV claims this 'creates the political shape of modern China'; omitted as overstated.

events.name: Huns Arrive in Europe
events.description: The Huns, nomadic horsemen from the steppes, overwhelm the Ostrogoths and drive the Visigoths across the Danube into the Roman Empire. The upheaval sets off the great migrations that help bring down the Western Roman Empire.
events.note: 375 is the conventional date. Related: attila-hun-invasions (450).

events.name: Chandragupta II Vikramaditya Takes the Throne
events.description: Chandragupta II, remembered by the title Vikramaditya, becomes emperor of the Gupta Empire. His reign extends Gupta power across northern and western India and is associated with a flowering of Sanskrit literature, art and science.
events.note: Accession dates vary (c. 375-380). Related: gupta-empire.

events.name: Founding of the Benedictine Order
events.description: Benedict of Nursia establishes the monastery of Monte Cassino in Italy, where he writes the Rule that becomes the model for Western monastic life. Benedictine monasteries go on to preserve learning and shape religious life across medieval Europe.
events.note: c. 529. CSV details mention his earlier monasteries at Subiaco.

events.name: Death of the Prophet Muhammad
events.description: The Prophet Muhammad dies in Medina, having united much of the Arabian Peninsula under Islam. The dispute over his succession, beginning with the choice of Abu Bakr as the first caliph, later shapes the division between Sunni and Shia Muslims.
events.note: CSV also says 'Beginning of Hijri Era', but that begins in 622 (existing hijra), so it is omitted. Related: islamic-caliphate-expands (632).

events.name: Mihira Bhoja Becomes King of Kannauj
events.description: Mihira Bhoja ascends the throne of the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty, ruling from Kannauj. Over a long reign he makes the Pratiharas one of the leading powers of northern India and a barrier against Arab expansion from Sindh.

events.name: Mahmud of Ghazni Takes Power
events.description: Mahmud becomes ruler of the Ghaznavid state in present-day Afghanistan and builds an empire stretching from eastern Iran to the Punjab. His repeated raids into northern India bring enormous wealth to his capital at Ghazni.
events.note: Related: mahmud-ghazni-somnath (1026).

events.name: Construction of the Tower of London Begins
events.description: William the Conqueror begins building the White Tower in London, a stone keep meant to dominate the city after the Norman Conquest. It grows into the Tower of London, serving over the centuries as royal palace, prison, armoury and home of the Crown Jewels.
events.note: 1078 is the usual start date.

events.name: University of Paris Emerges
events.description: Teachers and students attached to the cathedral school of Notre-Dame in Paris form a corporation that becomes the University of Paris. It grows into the leading centre of theology and philosophy in medieval Europe and a model for later universities.
events.note: c. 1150; the royal charter dates from 1200. Related: university-of-bologna-founded.

events.name: Qutb ud-Din Aibak Founds the Delhi Sultanate
events.description: After the death of Muhammad of Ghor, his former slave general Qutb ud-Din Aibak takes power in northern India and becomes the first sultan of Delhi. His Mamluk, or Slave, dynasty begins more than three centuries of sultanate rule.
events.note: Same start year as span delhi-sultanate (1206-1526): candidate for the event/span identity decision.

events.name: Razia Sultana Takes the Throne of Delhi
events.description: Razia, daughter of Sultan Iltutmish, becomes ruler of the Delhi Sultanate, the only woman ever to hold its throne. She governs actively and appears in public in male dress, but opposition from the Turkic nobility leads to her overthrow and death within four years.

events.name: Alauddin Khalji Becomes Sultan of Delhi
events.description: Alauddin Khalji seizes the throne of Delhi after having his uncle, Sultan Jalaluddin, killed. He repels repeated Mongol invasions, introduces strict price controls and land-revenue reforms, and extends the sultanate's power deep into southern India.

events.name: Muhammad bin Tughlaq Becomes Sultan
events.description: Muhammad bin Tughlaq becomes sultan of Delhi. A learned but erratic ruler, he is remembered for ambitious schemes that failed, including moving the capital to Daulatabad in the Deccan and issuing a token copper currency.
events.note: CSV row 1327 (capital moved to Daulatabad) is a likely related row.

events.name: Firuz Shah Tughlaq Becomes Sultan
events.description: Firuz Shah Tughlaq succeeds his cousin Muhammad bin Tughlaq as sultan of Delhi. His long reign is remembered for public works such as canals, new towns and the Feroz Shah Kotla citadel, even as the sultanate's power declines.

events.name: Babur Becomes Ruler of Ferghana
events.description: Babur, a Timurid prince descended from both Timur and Genghis Khan, inherits the small kingdom of Ferghana in Central Asia at about the age of eleven. Repeatedly driven from his homeland, he eventually turns south and founds the Mughal Empire in India.
events.note: Region uncertain: Ferghana is in Central Asia, which has no legacy label; South Asia was chosen because of his Mughal story. Related: babur-founds-mughal-empire.

events.name: First Portable Watches
events.description: Craftsmen in Nuremberg, notably the locksmith Peter Henlein, build small spring-driven clocks that can be carried on the person. These early watches begin the long shift towards personal, regular timekeeping that modern commerce and administration depend on.
events.note: Henlein's work is usually dated c. 1505-1510 and the attribution is debated.

events.name: Humayun Succeeds Babur
events.description: Babur, founder of the Mughal Empire, dies in Agra and is succeeded by his son Humayun. Humayun inherits a young, unsettled empire and soon faces challenges from his own brothers and from the Afghan leader Sher Shah Suri.

events.name: Humayun Recaptures Delhi
events.description: After fifteen years in exile, Humayun returns with Persian help, defeats the Suri dynasty and retakes Delhi, restoring Mughal rule. He dies months later after a fall on the steps of his library, leaving the throne to his young son Akbar.
events.note: Related: humayun-defeated-kanauj (1540), second-battle-of-panipat (1556).

events.name: Death of Akbar
events.description: Akbar the Great dies at Agra after nearly fifty years on the throne, having built the Mughal Empire into the dominant power of the subcontinent. His son Salim succeeds him as the emperor Jahangir.

events.name: Execution of Guru Arjan
events.description: Guru Arjan, the fifth Sikh Guru and compiler of the Adi Granth, is arrested on the orders of the Mughal emperor Jahangir and dies in custody after refusing to convert to Islam. Remembered as the first Sikh martyr, his death leads his successor to militarise the Sikh community.

events.name: Jahangir Marries Nur Jahan
events.description: The Mughal emperor Jahangir marries Mehr-un-Nissa, who receives the title Nur Jahan, 'Light of the World'. She becomes the most powerful woman in Mughal history, issuing coins and orders in her own name as real power passes to her in Jahangir's later years.

events.name: Death of Jahangir
events.description: The Mughal emperor Jahangir dies while travelling back from Kashmir. After a brief succession struggle his son Khurram takes the throne as Shah Jahan, the emperor who will build the Taj Mahal.
events.note: Split from a CSV row that bundles two events (see birth-of-shivaji).

events.name: Birth of Shivaji
events.description: Shivaji Bhonsle is born at the hill fort of Shivneri near Pune. He grows up to challenge the Mughal Empire and the Deccan sultanates, and is later crowned Chhatrapati of a new Maratha kingdom.
events.note: CHECK THE YEAR before approving. The CSV says 1627, but most sources now give 1630 (Maharashtra officially uses 19 Feb 1630). Split from a bundled CSV row. Related: shivaji-crowned-chhatrapati (1674).

events.name: Execution of Guru Tegh Bahadur
events.description: Guru Tegh Bahadur, the ninth Sikh Guru, is publicly executed in Delhi on the orders of the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb after refusing to convert to Islam. Sikhs remember him for defending freedom of religion, including that of Kashmiri Hindus.

events.name: Battle of Blenheim
events.description: An Anglo-Austrian army under the Duke of Marlborough and Prince Eugene of Savoy crushes a Franco-Bavarian force at Blenheim in Bavaria. The victory saves Vienna, knocks Bavaria out of the War of the Spanish Succession and ends the image of French invincibility.

events.name: Death of Guru Gobind Singh
aliases: Guru Granth Sahib as eternal Guru
events.description: Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Sikh Guru and founder of the Khalsa, dies at Nanded in the Deccan after being attacked. Before his death he declares that the line of human Gurus ends and that the scripture, the Guru Granth Sahib, will be the Sikhs' eternal Guru.

events.name: Nadir Shah Sacks Delhi
events.description: Nadir Shah of Persia defeats the Mughal army at Karnal and sacks Delhi, massacring thousands of its inhabitants. He carries off enormous treasure, including the Peacock Throne and the Koh-i-Noor diamond, exposing the weakness of the declining Mughal Empire.

events.name: Battle of Buxar
events.description: East India Company troops under Hector Munro defeat the combined forces of the Nawab of Bengal, the Nawab of Awadh and the Mughal emperor Shah Alam II. The victory leads to the Treaty of Allahabad, which gives the Company the right to collect revenue in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.
events.note: Related: battle-of-plassey (1757), east-india-company-bengal.

events.name: Second Anglo-Mysore War Begins
events.description: Hyder Ali of Mysore invades the Carnatic and inflicts a heavy defeat on East India Company forces at Pollilur. The war continues under his son Tipu Sultan after Hyder's death and ends with the Treaty of Mangalore, which restores the pre-war borders.
events.note: Related: tipu-sultan-killed (1799).

events.name: Robert Street Patents an Internal Combustion Engine
events.description: The English inventor Robert Street patents an engine that burns liquid fuel inside a cylinder, one of the earliest internal combustion designs. Practical internal combustion engines arrive only decades later, with the work of Lenoir, Otto and Benz.
events.note: The CSV calls this 'Invention of the Internal Combustion Engine', which is disputed. The draft is narrowed to the specific patent the CSV details describe.

events.name: Lewis and Clark Expedition
events.description: Meriwether Lewis and William Clark lead the Corps of Discovery up the Missouri River and across the Rocky Mountains to the Pacific coast, guided in part by the Shoshone woman Sacagawea. The expedition maps newly acquired western lands and strengthens American claims to the Pacific Northwest.
events.note: Two CSV rows: 178 says 1803 (Lewis set out down the Ohio) and 179 says 1804 (the expedition left the St. Louis area in May 1804). Used 1804.

events.name: Death of Napoleon
events.description: Napoleon Bonaparte dies in exile on the remote South Atlantic island of Saint Helena, where the British have held him since Waterloo. His legend, and the legal reforms of the Napoleonic Code, long outlive him.
events.note: Related: napoleon-defeat-waterloo (1815).

events.name: Indian Removal Act
events.description: President Andrew Jackson signs the Indian Removal Act, authorising the forced relocation of Native American nations from the southeastern United States to lands west of the Mississippi. The removals that follow, including the Cherokee 'Trail of Tears', cost thousands of lives.

events.name: United States Buys Alaska
events.description: The United States buys Alaska from the Russian Empire for 7.2 million dollars, in a deal negotiated by Secretary of State William Seward. Mocked at the time as 'Seward's Folly', the purchase ends Russia's presence in North America and later proves rich in gold and oil.

events.name: Stanley Finds Livingstone
events.description: The journalist Henry Morton Stanley, sent by the New York Herald, finds the missing Scottish missionary and explorer David Livingstone at Ujiji on Lake Tanganyika. His reported greeting, 'Dr. Livingstone, I presume?', becomes one of the most famous lines in the history of exploration.

events.name: Battle of the Little Bighorn
events.description: Lakota Sioux and Northern Cheyenne warriors led by Sitting Bull and Crazy Horse destroy Lieutenant Colonel George Custer's detachment of the 7th Cavalry in Montana. The victory is short-lived: the US Army responds with an intensified campaign that forces the Plains nations onto reservations.

events.name: Edison Demonstrates the Light Bulb
events.description: Thomas Edison and his team at Menlo Park demonstrate a long-lasting incandescent lamp with a carbon filament. Edison's work on bulbs, and on the power stations to supply them, helps bring electric light into homes and cities around the world.
events.note: Joseph Swan developed a similar lamp in parallel in England.

events.name: Benz Builds the First Practical Automobile
events.description: Karl Benz builds his three-wheeled Patent-Motorwagen in Mannheim, powered by a petrol engine of his own design, and patents it early the following year. It is widely regarded as the first practical automobile and begins a transformation of transport, cities and industry.
events.note: Built 1885, patented January 1886.

events.name: Spanish–American War
events.description: After the battleship USS Maine explodes in Havana harbour, the United States goes to war with Spain over Cuba. In a few months of fighting the US defeats Spain and gains Puerto Rico, Guam and the Philippines, emerging as a colonial power in the Pacific and the Caribbean.

events.name: Eisenhower Elected US President
events.description: Dwight D. Eisenhower, the general who commanded Allied forces in Europe during the Second World War, wins the US presidential election for the Republicans. His two terms see the end of the Korean War, the start of the Interstate Highway System and a deepening Cold War.

events.name: Silicon Integrated Circuit Invented
events.description: Robert Noyce at Fairchild Semiconductor devises a practical silicon integrated circuit, building on Jack Kilby's demonstration of an integrated circuit at Texas Instruments the year before. Packing many components onto a single chip makes possible the modern computer and the digital age.
events.note: Kilby 1958 (germanium), Noyce 1959 (silicon).

events.name: France Tests Its First Atomic Bomb
events.description: France explodes its first nuclear device, code-named Gerboise Bleue, in the Algerian Sahara and becomes the world's fourth nuclear power. The test reflects President de Gaulle's determination to give France a nuclear deterrent independent of the United States.
events.note: Region chosen by the actor (France); the test site is in Algeria (Africa).

events.name: Federation of Malaysia Formed
events.description: Malaya joins with Singapore, Sabah and Sarawak to form the Federation of Malaysia under Prime Minister Tunku Abdul Rahman. The new state faces armed 'Confrontation' from Indonesia, and Singapore leaves the federation within two years.
events.note: Region: Southeast Asia, filed under East Asia per existing convention (Vietnam War, Khmer Rouge).

events.name: Partial Nuclear Test Ban Treaty Signed
events.description: The United States, the Soviet Union and Britain sign a treaty in Moscow banning nuclear weapons tests in the atmosphere, in outer space and under water. Signed months after the Cuban Missile Crisis, it is the first major arms-control agreement of the Cold War.

events.name: Cosmic Microwave Background Discovered
events.description: Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson of Bell Labs detect a faint microwave signal coming evenly from every direction in the sky. It turns out to be radiation left over from the early universe, providing strong evidence for the Big Bang theory and later earning them a Nobel Prize.

events.name: Singapore Becomes Independent
events.description: Singapore is separated from the Federation of Malaysia and becomes a sovereign city-state, with Lee Kuan Yew as prime minister. Despite having few natural resources, it grows into one of the world's wealthiest trading hubs.
events.note: Region: Southeast Asia, filed under East Asia per existing convention.

events.name: Death of Winston Churchill
events.description: Sir Winston Churchill, Britain's prime minister for most of the Second World War, dies in London at the age of ninety. He is given a state funeral, an honour rarely granted to anyone outside the royal family.

events.name: Jimmy Carter Elected US President
events.description: Jimmy Carter, a former peanut farmer and governor of Georgia, defeats Gerald Ford in the first presidential election after the Watergate scandal. His presidency brings the Camp David Accords but also economic troubles and the Iran hostage crisis.

events.name: Seychelles Gains Independence
events.description: The Seychelles, an archipelago in the Indian Ocean, becomes independent from Britain as a republic within the Commonwealth, with James Mancham as its first president. A coup the following year brings France-Albert René to power.

events.name: Khmer Rouge Driven from Phnom Penh
events.description: Vietnamese forces, together with Cambodian rebels opposed to Pol Pot, capture Phnom Penh and drive the Khmer Rouge from power. A Vietnamese-backed government takes over, while the Khmer Rouge retreat to the jungle and fight on for nearly two decades.
events.note: CSV says 'Cambodian rebels grab power'; the rebels came to power through a Vietnamese invasion. Related: khmer-rouge-cambodia (1975).

events.name: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto Executed
events.description: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, Pakistan's former prime minister and founder of the Pakistan People's Party, is hanged after a disputed murder trial under the military government of General Zia-ul-Haq. His death makes him a martyr to his supporters, and his daughter Benazir later leads the party.

events.name: United States Invades Grenada
events.description: After a coup in which Grenada's prime minister Maurice Bishop is killed, US forces invade the small Caribbean island in Operation Urgent Fury. The intervention, condemned by the UN General Assembly, removes the military government within days.
events.note: The CSV row also mentions the US withdrawal from UNESCO (announced 1983, effective 1984), which is not drafted.

events.name: United States Bombs Libya
events.description: US warplanes strike targets in Tripoli and Benghazi in retaliation for a bombing at a Berlin disco that Washington blames on Libya. The raid, aimed at Muammar Gaddafi's regime, deepens the confrontation between Libya and the West.

events.name: Palestinian Declaration of Independence
events.description: Meeting in Algiers, the Palestine National Council led by Yasser Arafat proclaims an independent State of Palestine. The declaration implicitly accepts a two-state solution and is soon recognised by many countries, though the territory remains under Israeli occupation.

events.name: Spitak Earthquake in Armenia
events.description: A powerful earthquake devastates northern Soviet Armenia, destroying the town of Spitak and much of Leninakan and killing tens of thousands of people. For the first time, the Soviet Union openly accepts large-scale aid from the West.
events.note: The CSV says nearly 100,000 were killed; most estimates are 25,000-50,000, so the draft gives no figure. Region uncertain (Caucasus); Europe chosen, as for other Soviet events.

events.name: Zia-ul-Haq Killed in Plane Crash
events.description: General Muhammad Zia-ul-Haq, Pakistan's military ruler since he overthrew Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, dies when his plane crashes near Bahawalpur, along with the US ambassador. Elections later that year bring Benazir Bhutto to power.
events.note: The CSV row bundles four 1988 items; only this one is drafted. The others are WHO's no-smoking day, the French president's re-election and an earthquake in Bihar.

events.name: UN Transition to Namibian Independence Begins
events.description: UN peacekeepers of the Transition Assistance Group begin carrying out Security Council Resolution 435, overseeing South Africa's withdrawal and free elections in Namibia. The process ends decades of South African rule, and Namibia becomes independent the following year.

events.name: India Refuses to Sign the Test Ban Treaty
events.description: India refuses to sign the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty, objecting that it does not commit the nuclear powers to disarmament, and blocks its adoption at the Conference on Disarmament. The treaty is instead adopted through the UN General Assembly; two years later India carries out nuclear tests.
events.note: Related: pokhran-nuclear-tests.

events.name: Sheikh Hasina Becomes Prime Minister
events.description: Sheikh Hasina, leader of the Awami League and daughter of Bangladesh's founding leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, becomes prime minister for the first time. She goes on to become the country's longest-serving head of government.

events.name: Kofi Annan Chosen as UN Secretary-General
events.description: The Ghanaian diplomat Kofi Annan is appointed Secretary-General of the United Nations, the first to rise from within the UN's own staff. He later shares the Nobel Peace Prize with the UN for work on peace and human rights.
events.note: Appointed December 1996; took office January 1997.

events.name: Suharto Resigns
events.description: Indonesian President Suharto resigns after more than three decades in power, following the Asian financial crisis, mass protests and riots. His fall opens the Reformasi era of democratic reform in the world's largest Muslim-majority country.
events.note: Split from a bundled CSV row (see clinton-impeached). Region: Southeast Asia, filed under East Asia per existing convention.

events.name: Bill Clinton Impeached
events.description: The US House of Representatives impeaches President Bill Clinton on charges of perjury and obstruction of justice arising from his affair with Monica Lewinsky. The Senate acquits him early the following year and he completes his second term.
events.note: The CSV says 'faces impeachment'; the House vote came in December 1998. The same row mentions Pakistan's Ghauri missile test, which is not drafted.

events.name: Yugoslavia Accepts Kosovo Peace Plan
events.description: After eleven weeks of NATO air strikes, Yugoslav President Slobodan Milošević accepts an international peace plan and withdraws Serbian forces from Kosovo. A NATO-led force and a UN administration take over the province, which later declares independence.

csv_triage.note: Same expedition as row 179; merged into one draft (see its note on 1803 vs 1804).
DATE CONFLICT: CSV says c. 3000 BC, the app says 2560 BCE (the span construction-great-pyramid is -2580..-2560).
DATE CONFLICT: CSV says c. 576 BC, the app says 563 BCE. Row 20 gives a third date.
DATE CONFLICT: CSV says 486 BC, row 15 says c. 576 BC, the app says 563 BCE. Scholarly estimates range from c. 563 to c. 480 BCE.
Spelling variant (Vijayanagar). Missed by the matcher; worth adding 'Vijayanagar' as an alias.
Covered by the time span construction-eiffel-tower (1887..1889).
'The period of Aristotle and Plato' is an era, not a datable event. Could become a time span.
'Roger Bacon invents gunpowder' conflicts with gunpowder-invented (c. 850, China). Bacon described a recipe c. 1267 but did not invent it.
'Military Aid Pact between China and Pakistan, 1954' looks wrong: the 1954 pact was between the US and Pakistan. Check before using.
Security Council presidency rotates monthly; too minor for the game.
